baseline.limitation: Recent changes are not separate commits; exact day-by-day attribution is unavailable.

changesSinceBaseline: The earlier single search-and-answer flow was split into research, private composition and mandatory private final review.
The final review can approve, revise or withhold a draft based on purpose, perspective, relevance, safety, evidence and tone.
Answer instructions became shorter: generally forty to ninety words, with a ninety-word review target and a one-hundred-word server ceiling.
Relevance, numbered citations, conversational feedback handling and the prohibition on routine doctor questions were tightened.
A fixed-topic-only search restriction protected private content but lost important intent, including childbirth duration.

The latest approved change replaces that search restriction with private preparation of a full general question using relevant conversational context. Reports and original conversation are excluded from research.
confirmedBug: The previous topic mapper reduced how-long-childbirth-takes to labour and childbirth; the spaced spelling child birth could miss that mapping too.
uncertainty: The exact failed review check in the visitor screenshot is unavailable. The fixed refusal proves withholding, not which check failed.
safety: Urgent guidance, personal-result interpretation boundaries, medical decisions and purpose review remain in force.

limitations: AI preparation can make mistakes; the notice explicitly says so. Checks reject invalid output, numeric values, addresses, URLs and failed privacy/intent flags; these are not a proof that arbitrary sensitive text can never escape.
Direct live inspection of the internal preparation action failed in the CLI. Integration tests inspect the outgoing research request; live app checks exercise the normal answer path.
This work is not a complete audit of all acceptance tests, medical accuracy, provider retention or spending controls.
Live checks establish substantive replies and context handling in the tested cases. They are not a clinical-accuracy certification or a guarantee that the model will never withhold another reply.
